29598edb-6e54-4477-9761-9e5f4b61bdeb.description: Error ratio over 5m is above 14.4x the 1% error budget (fast burn); at this rate a 30-day budget lasts about 2 days.

facts.statement: checkout error ratio (5m) was 0.3225 at 19:28:03, rising from 0.1422 at 19:26:33.
checkout's errors are PaymentService/Charge dial failures: 'dial tcp 10.96.254.222:9999: i/o timeout'. The error propagates to frontend and frontend-proxy as HTTP 500s.
checkout revision 2, created 19:25:44, has change cause 'payment client moved to port 9999'. The diff changes PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999.
checkout's own logs show no error-level lines in the window.
payment has one revision (created 19:11:42), is Available with 1/1 ready, and its pod events show no warnings.
payment's logs are all info and stop at 19:25:43. Its server Charge span rate falls to 0 by 19:28.
No feature flags are on, so flags do not explain the incident.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check payment's Service and container ports in the otel-demo namespace, and confirm no listener on 9999 (for example, a port-forward or nc from a checkout pod).
hypotheses.statement: Payment's service port is 8080 and nothing listens on 9999. The payment side is unchanged.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Run kubectl rollout undo on checkout, then check service:sli_error_ratio:rate5m for checkout and the payment Charge server span rate.
hypotheses.statement: Rolling checkout back to revision 1 should clear the errors within about a minute.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Break checkout's error ratio down by span_name and check the PlaceOrder server span error ratio over the same window.
hypotheses.statement: The 7% checkout client error ratio on the Charge span is lower than the 32% overall checkout ratio. Other failing paths may exist, or the rate windows differ.

inferences.statement: The checkout config change moved the payment address to a port payment does not serve. Checkout's charge calls fail, causing the checkout error burn and the downstream frontend and frontend-proxy errors. Payment is not the root cause.

root_causes.cause: Bad config release (revision 2, 'payment client moved to port 9999') changed PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999. Payment does not answer on that port, so every charge dial times out and checkout returns errors.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout is failing about 32% of requests (fast burn). The errors start at 19:26, right after checkout revision 2 went out at 19:25:44. That revision changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls fail with TCP dial i/o timeouts to 10.96.254.222:9999. Payment is healthy on its own side: single revision, pod running, no warnings, no error logs. Its traffic dropped to zero after the change. Frontend and frontend-proxy errors are downstream of checkout. The likely fix is to roll checkout back to revision 1 or correct the payment port.

actions.reason: Checkout revision 2 (19:25:44, 'payment client moved to port 9999') changed PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999. Charge calls time out dialing 10.96.254.222:9999, and errors start right after the release. Revision 1 restores payment:8080.

alternatives.why_not: Checkout's logs show no fault in the process, and a restart would keep the bad PAYMENT_ADDR from revision 2, so the errors would continue.
The failures are dial timeouts to a wrong port, not a capacity problem, so more replicas would not help.
Leaving it would keep the checkout fast burn going (about 2 days of 30-day budget at this rate). Rollback is the supported fix.

plan.summary: Roll checkout back from revision 2 (PAYMENT_ADDR moved to payment:9999, which payment does not serve) to revision 1 (payment:8080). Checkout's Charge dials should succeed again, and the error burn and downstream frontend/frontend-proxy 500s should clear; verify the checkout error ratio drops after the rollback.
